body:
This is certainly an improvement for this case, but it does come with some drawbacks.

What this math in either case is doing is just assuming a certain distance between the interface and the object behind it. In the current code, it's using a value that depends on the distance from the camera to the interface, and you're advocating for (close to) a constant distance instead.

A constant distance is correct if you tune your refraction for a single object, but if you have objects with a variety of scales, the effect shows its weaknesses. Scaling up the demo to be massive will show that there's now effectively no refraction at all for what *was* a correct refraction value at the smaller scale.

The proposed fix as currently written also introduces a strong dependence on the value of the near plane, which refraction values would need to be tuned specifically for. 

Personally, I think this probably works better in more common cases than the current behavior, but it's not entirely clear cut.

Refraction should correct for aspect ratio. Currently resizing the screen can affect it and that's not right IMO.

I dislike assuming a constant distance from the interface, but one that can be tweaked from the Material is welcome. It can be modelled as a ray-plane intersection against the screen texture. 

For inspiration see a breakdown of [this effect](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/uLN69rtiu4Y) from Portal 2.
